Article Title: 'Women police personnel molested': Centre's charge puts Rahul Gandhi-led protest in focus
Article Text:
Centre flags alleged incidents amid Rahul Gandhi row

NEW DELHI: The Centre on Friday defended the security measures and restrictions imposed in Delhi ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party’s planned protest on October 10, telling the Supreme Court that the steps were necessary to ensure the safety of residents.However, the court expressed concern over the disruption to public transport, cautioning authorities against going overboard in the name of security.Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre, argued that law enforcement agencies had to take preventive measures in view of the planned demonstration against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Referring to recent protests in the national capital, Centre alleged that "women police personnel had been molested, attacked and injured," over the last few days.The submission brought Congress leader Rahul Gandhi into the spotlight once again, after the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party accused the leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha of behaving “inappropriately” with a woman police officer during a protest a day earlier.BJP leader Kesavan had criticised Rahul over the alleged incident, asking, “How can any decent individual, let alone a member of parliament or a leader of the opposition, behave in such an inappropriate manner with a woman, and that too, a female police personnel?”However, the top court questioned the extent of the restrictions imposed in the capital, particularly the proposed closure of Metro stations and disruption to railway services ahead of Saturday’s protest.“Exercise caution, there's nothing wrong with that. Police are responsible for maintaining law and order,” the court observed on the security arrangements for the October 10 demonstration.Taking up the issue of Metro station closures, the court cautioned that security measures should not bring daily life to a standstill.“Law enforcement agencies can't bring everything to halt & leave people without any transport facility,” it said.The court also questioned whether the restrictions were proportionate to the threat, remarking, “One should not use hammer to kill fly,” while referring to the closure of Delhi Metro stations ahead of the CJP protest.The hearing came amid heightened security across the national capital, with authorities stepping up arrangements and imposing restrictions in wake of the October 10 protest demanding Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation.
Article Summary: The Centre told the Supreme Court that the steps were necessary to ensure the safety of residents. The court expressed concern over the disruption to public transport, cautioning authorities against going overboard in the name of security. The hearing came amid heightened security across the national capital, with authorities stepping up arrangements.

Article Title: FIR against Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi over 'assault' during anti-Gyanesh Kumar protest in Delhi
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi during protest.

NEW DELHI: Delhi Police has registered an FIR against Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra for allegedly assaulting police personnel and obstructing government work during a protest in the capital, news agency PTI reported, citing police sources on Thursday.The FIR invokes various sections related to allegedly assaulting and manhandling police personnel, obstructing public servants in the discharge of their duties and misbehaviour with police officers.The action comes a day after INDIA bloc MPs were stopped by Delhi Police while attempting to march towards Jantar Mantar for a protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Several other Congress leaders and party workers who took part in the demonstration have also been named in the FIR, police sources said.Police are examining the allegations and the role of those involved in the protest.Earlier on Wednesday, Rahul, Priyanka had led INDIA bloc leaders in a street protest, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Police detained 91 people during the demonstration, including several MPs and other political leaders.The protest took an intense turn after police stopped the protesters while they were travelling in buses towards Jantar Mantar for a surprise sit-in.The leaders had earlier attended a lunch meeting at a South Indian vegetarian restaurant on Janpath.Priyanka and several other women leaders lay on the road holding copies of the Constitution. They were later removed and taken away in police buses as opposition members raised slogans.MPs from the Congress, Trinamool Congress, CPM, CPI, RJD, IUML and several other parties were among those participating in the protest.
Article Summary: Rahul, Priyanka led INDIA bloc leaders in a street protest, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Police detained 91 people during the demonstration, including several MPs and other political leaders. Police are examining the allegations and the role of those involved in the protest.

Article Title: 'Did not follow lawful directions earlier': Why Delhi Police denied permission for CJP's October 10 protest
Article Text:
Delhi Police denies CJP permission for Oct 10 protest, cites late application and past violations

NEW DELHI: The Delhi Police has denied permission for the Cockroach Janata Party’s (CJP) proposed protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10, citing the late submission of its application, non-compliance with rules during a previous demonstration and concerns over public safety, law and order, and traffic management.Addressing a press conference, Joint Commissioner of Police Nupur Prasad said the New Delhi district police received an application from CJP co-convenor Saurabh Das on October 7, seeking permission to hold a protest demanding accountability from Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.“On October 7, 2026, an application from Saurabh Das, Co-Convenor of the Cockroach Janata Party, was received in the New Delhi District. As per the application, an intimation was given regarding a protest to be held at Jantar Mantar on October 10 concerning the accountability of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC). Upon processing this intimation, it was found that the notice was received at very short notice. Under current guidelines, an application to organise an event at Jantar Mantar must be submitted at least 10 days prior to the scheduled date.It is also important to note that, based on the past conduct of the CJP on a separate occasion, undertakings and lawful directions given previously were not followed," Prasad said."In light of the non-compliance with prescribed procedures, the failure to adhere to past legal directions, and the current state of public safety, law and order, and traffic regulation, permission for the proposed protest at Jantar Mantar is hereby denied,” she added.Meanwhile, the Supreme Court has rejected a plea seeking directions to give Delhi Police a free hand to deal with protesters, observing that the future of young students and their families must be considered in such matters.A bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said many protesters were young and should not be unnecessarily drawn into prolonged court proceedings.“These are young students and protesters before us. We have to see their parents, we have to see they have a long life. [They should not be] entangled with court hearings etc.,” the CJI said.The court, however, clarified that its earlier orders protecting protesters did not extend to those alleged to be hardened criminals or accused of serious offences.
Article Summary: The Delhi Police has denied permission for the Cockroach Janata Party’s (CJP) proposed protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10. The police cited the late submission of its application, non-compliance with rules during a previous demonstration and concerns over public safety, law and order, and traffic management.

Article Title: 'Calculated campaign driven by vested political interests': 42 ex-judges back Gyanesh Kumar in open letter

NEW DELHI: A total of 42 former judges on Thursday expressed deep concern over protests targeting Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, saying he had been labelled a "puppet", "thief" and "compromised" in what they described as a "calculated campaign driven by vested political interests".In an open letter, the veterans took strong exception to officers, who conduct the elections, being called names and shamed with "warning of reprisal once power changes hands"."This appears to be a calculated campaign driven by vested political interests, with little regard for the potentially devastating consequences of destabilising the world’s largest democracy," the 42 veterans said."Activist outfits with a long record of selective litigation lend these claims a veneer of legality. They file petition, one after the other. They seldom file proof," the letter said in an apparent attack on CJP, which has been levelling serious charges against CEC Gyanesh Kumar over a reported dissent within the poll body.Veterans also said that "criticism of institutions is a democratic right. Denigration is not".They also hit out at the Congress party , which has doubled down on its verbal assault on Gyanesh Kumar, by questioning how the party's victory through the same EVM goes unquestioned.The ex-service members also highlighted how ECI's demand for sworn declaration was not submitted by the Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi."A party that governed this nation for over five decades now claims that the very system which elected it is rigged. It does not act alone. Activist outfits with a long record of selective litigation lend these claims a veneer of legality. They file petition, one after the other. They seldom file proof," they wrote in a letter.This comes as Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, after hosting a lunch for INDIA bloc leaders for the second consecutive day, declared that the opposition would be heading to Gandhi Memorial for a peaceful sit-in.Whereas, Rahul Gandhi again attacked Gyanesh Kumar, along with PM Modi, home minister Amit Shah and RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat, accusing them of "hijacking democracy" through criminal conspiracy.The party on Thursday said the opposition was fighting to protect democracy, voters, and the common people of the country.The development comes amid the opposition's ongoing protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Kharge hosted the lunch for INDIA bloc leaders at a restaurant in the national capital on Thursday.Meanwhile, CJP founder Abhijit Dipke accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of "murdering democracy and vote theft," and said protests will go on till CEC Gyanesh Kumar resigns from his post.Presiding over a protest held by civil society group and CJP here against SIR, he alleged that voter deletions under the Special Intensive Revision were aimed at disenfranchising those opposed to the BJP and accused PM Modi and the Election Commission of murdering democracy and causing vote theft.
Article Summary: 42 former judges express deep concern over protests targeting Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. They say he has been labelled a "puppet", "thief" and "compromised" in what they described as a "calculated campaign driven by vested political interests"

Article Title: FIR registered after Kashmiri youth alleges assault at Connaught Place protest
Article Text:
FIR filed over alleged assault on Kashmiri youth as Delhi tightens security ahead of protests

NEW DELHI: Delhi police on Friday registered an FIR against unknown persons following a complaint by a Kashmiri youth who was allegedly assaulted at Connaught Place during as the Congress was protesting against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.The Kashmiri youth, who said he was a fan of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, was allegedly roughed up by protesters at Connaught Place. The protesters claimed he had verbally abused Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, as cited by ANI.The youth denied abusing Gandhi and said, “I raised a question - when the Opposition wins, then there are no problems with the EVMs. Who brought EVMs? It was Rajiv Gandhi in 1998. I am from Kashmir. I did not abuse Rahul Gandhi. I am a citizen of this country and I will not let this country become another Nepal.”Delhi Police has stepped up security across the national capital ahead of the INDIA bloc’s Friday march to Rashtrapati Bhavan, where opposition leaders are expected to seek President Droupadi Murmu’s intervention over their demand for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation, sources said.More than 20,000 police and paramilitary personnel have been deployed across central Delhi, with security strengthened around Parliament, Connaught Place, Jantar Mantar and other sensitive locations. Police teams are monitoring potential gathering points and routes leading to Rashtrapati Bhavan, while additional Central Armed Police Forces personnel have been mobilised to guard key roads. Pickets and barricades have also been placed at strategic points.The heightened security comes ahead of a proposed Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) protest on Saturday against Kumar. Delhi Police has warned that the gathering would be illegal while restrictions under Section 163 remain in force.Deputy Commissioner of Police Shrishti Pandey said protests were not permitted at Jantar Mantar or any other location during this period and warned that unauthorised gatherings would invite legal action.“Section 163 is in effect, meaning protests are not permitted—neither at Jantar Mantar nor anywhere else. Any gathering will be considered illegal, and we would be compelled to take necessary legal action against it,” Pandey said.She urged people not to participate in the proposed protest, asking them to prioritise their safety and that of their families.
Article Summary: FIR filed over alleged assault on Kashmiri youth as Delhi tightens security ahead of protests. Delhi Police has stepped up security across the national capital ahead of the INDIA bloc’s Friday march to Rashtrapati Bhavan. More than 20,000 police and paramilitary personnel have been deployed across central Delhi.

NEW DELHI: Kerala high court on Friday ordered FIR registration under the anti-graft law against former chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan and others in connection with the alleged CMRL bribery case, based on a report submitted by the Enforcement Directorate Justice A Badharudeen allowed a petition filed by advocate K M Shajahan, who argued that the police should register an FIR instead of conducting a preliminary inquiry into the allegations in the ED report.A detailed judgment is awaited.The ED had told the court that an FIR could be registered against Vijayan, his daughter Veena T and her husband, P A Mohamed Riyas, based on the report it had submitted to the state police. NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) has accused Rajasthan Police of forcibly detaining its national organisational co-in-charge Deepak Baliyan from his residence in Alwar district and manhandling him despite his fractured leg, while police maintained that he had not been detained.The controversy comes ahead of the CJP's planned protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi on October 10, where the party is demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged manipulation of electoral rolls and the deletion of lakhs of voters' names during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.Baliyan, a resident of Mankheda village in Alwar district, had earlier accused local police of placing him under house arrest and threatening his family ahead of the protest. He alleged that police dragged Baliyan, who was recovering from a leg fracture, causing further injuries to his leg. Ranka also claimed that Baliyan was taken on a journey of around 100 km before being dropped back at his house.In a post on X, Ranka said, "Some boundaries shouldn't be crossed, and it's good that Rajasthan Police realised that eventually."In an earlier post, Ranka had accused Rajasthan Police of behaving like "goons" over the alleged treatment of Baliyan and his brother. He also called on party supporters to reach the Kathumar police station following the allegations.The CJP has maintained that the alleged police action was linked to its planned protest against Kumar over the revision of electoral rolls. Police, however, have denied detaining Baliyan.

Article Title: KPSC scam candidates taken to resorts, provided with Q&A: ED
Article Text:
Karnataka Public Service Commission recruitment process was manipulated through an organised mechanism to generate proceeds of crime, ED said

NEW DELHI: The Enforcement Directorate on Thursday claimed that in the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) paper leak case, candidates for the veterinary officers' exam were taken to resorts/Airbnb a day before the exam, provided test papers and their answer sheets, all for Rs 40 lakh per candidate.Two days ago, the agency had arrested KPSC ex-chairman Shivashankarappa and its member B V Geetha.Giving details of its investigation into alleged corruption in Karnataka PSC, the agency said Gyanendra Gangwar, the arrested IAS officer who was controller of examinations at KPSC, was in custody of confidential examination material and had leaked them to Geetha. The ED said an organised syndicate paid bribes to officials from top to bottom.The ED's probe by its Bengaluru unit is based on multiple FIRs registered by the police at Vidhana Soudha police station in the case of recruitment of 400 veterinary officers."Evidence gathered so far has revealed an organised mechanism for generation of proceeds of crime through manipulation of the KPSC recruitment process. KPSC officials leaked question papers and candidate specific answer keys," the ED added.ED searched the premises of former Shivashankarappa and Geetha on Oct 6, which was followed by their arrest."The searches resulted in seizure of blank signed cheques of Rs 80 lakh, along with blank signed promissory notes, from one of the successful candidates," the ED said. The agency has traced at least 10 successful candidates who were allegedly taken to a resort/Airbnb villa on the outskirts of Bengaluru a day before the examination, where they were provided with a question paper and correct answer options and made to practice/memorise them.According to the ED, the question paper (marked with correct answers) containing 80 questions was leaked by Gangwar through his close associate, Basavaraj Kannale, to these 10 candidates."Basavaraj Kannale has collected bribe money amounting to Rs 40-50 lakh from each candidate, in consideration of facilitating their final selection in the veterinary officers' recruitment exam," ED said.Gangwar and Kannale were arrested on Sept 17-18 and sent to ED custody for 14 days. "During ED custody, Gangwar disclosed crucial information relating to irregularities in conducting various KPSC recruitment exams," ED added.
Article Summary: The Enforcement Directorate said candidates for the veterinary officers' exam were taken to resorts/Airbnb a day before the exam. Two days ago, the agency had arrested KPSC ex-chairman Shivashankarappa and its member B V Geetha. The ED said an organised syndicate paid bribes to officials from top to bottom.

Article Title: File doesn't reach judge in time, Supreme Court adjourns hearing on Punjab appeal
Article Text:
Supreme Court said the state’s petition will be listed for hearing either Wednesday or Thursday

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday adjourned the hearing to Friday on Punjab govt's appeal against an HC directive for CBI probe into ED's allegations of corruption in transfers, postings and tenders allegedly perpetrated by an OSD to the CM as the case file did not reach one of the two judges scheduled to take up the case.Justice Dipankar Datta told senior advocate Vikas Singh, who appeared for the state, the case file did not reach his bench partner Justice Sheel Nagu on time for him to prepare for the hearing. "It can either be taken up on Friday or Monday."Singh preferred a hearing on Friday but urged SC to restrain CBI from taking any coercive action based on HC's Oct 5 order. Justice Datta asked, "How can we grant any interim order without hearing?" Singh said Justice Nagu, who was the Punjab and Haryana HC chief justice for two years until his SC elevation, had dealt with the person involved in some other case. Justice Nagu said he would go through the case file and decide whether to hear the case.
Article Summary: Supreme Court adjourned the hearing to Friday on Punjab govt's appeal against an HC directive for CBI probe into ED's allegations of corruption. The case file did not reach one of the two judges scheduled to take up the case. Justice Dipankar Datta told senior advocate Vikas Singh, who appeared for the state, the case file didn't reach his bench partner Justice Sheel Nagu.

Article Title: Proof of 21 'compromised transfers', 11 policy changes part of CBI's Punjab file
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: A day before the Supreme Court is scheduled to take up a plea for restraining its probe into allegations against OSD to Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann , CBI was learnt to be in possession of evidence of "compromised transfers" of at least 21 senior state govt and police officers of Punjab.The evidence, collected as part of its probe into the "cash-for-postings" scam, includes an alleged push for the transfer of a senior cop from the anti-gangster task force and the suspension of an officer of Sangrur jail. CBI, based on ED probe, has mentioned alleged instances of Mann's OSD Rajbir Singh Ghuman's role in its FIR against him.Eleven alleged instances of changes in policy, including bid to influence the transport policy and administrative decisions, have also been cited. The FIR mentions instances of request for issue of arms licences, including the one made to a senior IPS officer by Nitin Gohal, an accused in the case.Gohal allegedly had his brother, Jitin, also an accused, posted in CMO through Ghuman in Jan to act as a middleman. Gohal was questioned by ED in May regarding his alleged role in organising administrative favours, and tender manipulations across Punjab.Confronted with evidence containing numerous communications from officers, and MLAs requesting posting favours, Gohal pointed to his 22-year friendship with Ghuman.He said he merely performed "data entry type work", including compiling spreadsheets and forwarding them to CMO officials. Probe, however, found Gohal acquired an industrial plot in Mohali, financed equally by his business partner, after purchasing the land from Pritpal Dhindsa, who had similarly approached Gohal with transfer requests.The probe highlighted Gohal's dealings with rice sheller businessman R S Nagra. Evidence showed Nagra repeatedly approaching Gohal for transfers of officials. He sought Gohal's intervention to alter tender terms.
Article Summary: CBI learnt to be in possession of evidence of "compromised transfers" of at least 21 senior state govt and police officers of Punjab. Supreme Court is scheduled to take up a plea for restraining its probe into allegations against OSD to Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann.

Article Title: 4 FIRs against Rahul, Priyanka over anti-CEC protests in Delhi
Article Text:
The protests continued for a third consecutive day on Thursday

NEW DELHI: The Delhi Police has so far registered at least four FIRs against Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other opposition leaders in connection with the two-day protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in Lutyens' Delhi, sources told news agency PTI on Thursday.The FIRs were registered under sections relating to assault, obstructing public servants from discharging their duties and violation of Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), the sources told PTI. The development came a day after police registered an FIR against Rahul and Priyanka for allegedly forcing their way into Akashvani Bhawan. Police had detained 91 people, including several MPs, during Wednesday's protest.The opposition leaders had been stopped while attempting to march to Jantar Mantar for a sit-in demanding Kumar's resignation over allegations of "vote chori". Rahul Gandhi had earlier claimed that around 300 MPs wanted to hold a peaceful protest but were stopped by police and "beaten up".The protests continued for a third consecutive day on Thursday, with INDIA bloc leaders staging a sit-in at Mahatma Gandhi's memorial at Rajghat.The opposition has accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah and CEC Kumar of "hijacking" the country through an alleged conspiracy involving "vote chori".Rahul Gandhi said Modi, Shah, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat and Kumar had "destroyed the Constitution and stolen votes", asserting that they would be brought to justice."The truth is that Narendra Modi, Amit Shah, Mohan Bhagwat, and Gyanesh Kumar have hijacked the country through a criminal conspiracy. They have destroyed the Constitution and stolen votes," he said.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the opposition had come to Rajghat to pray for "wisdom" for the government and the Election Commission, while demanding that alleged irregularities in the electoral process be stopped.The opposition leaders are also seeking time to meet President Droupadi Murmu to present their case and demand Kumar's dismissal.Congress leaders and representatives of the CPI-M, CPI, TMC, RJD and SP said the agitation would continue on Friday. Sources said Friday's plan remains centred on Rashtrapati Bhavan, with a morning meeting scheduled at Parliament House.TMC chief Mamata Banerjee and SP leader Ram Gopal Yadav are expected to join Friday's proceedings.
Article Summary: Delhi Police has so far registered at least four FIRs against Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi. The development came a day after police registered an FIR against Rahul and Priyanka for allegedly forcing their way into Akashvani Bhawan. Police had detained 91 people, including several MPs, during Wednesday's protest.

Team of lawyer comrades are in touch with them.But if any lawyer can be at the PS immediately, pls DM."Rosie is among the three female journalists who filed complaint alleging sexual harassment by police personnel during a protest in the New Delhi area on October 3.The complants have been transferred to the Crime Branch at Kamla Market for further action.Delhi Police also detained several protesters outside Parliament Street Police Station who were demonstrating over an alleged incident of sexual misconduct involving three women journalists during an October 3 protest at Jantar Mantar.The protesters alleged that they had been demonstrating since 6pm on Sunday, demanding registration of an FIR in the case. Police detained them around 7am on Monday following a clash, with protesters alleging they were treated poorly despite only seeking registration of an FIR. Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Derek O’Brien also extended support to Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders as party spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka claimed that multiple sources had warned that the three could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other equivalent provisions.“With you all the way 🪳🪳stay strong. ‘10 Oct poora desh aa raha hai…’,” O’Brien said in a post on X while replying to Dipke.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacting to the claim said they would not be intimidated by the possibility of action under laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) or National Security Act (NSA).“If the Govt believes that the threat of UAPA, NSA or years behind bars will scare us into silence, it won’t,” Dipke said in a post on X, adding that the protesters were prepared to spend “months or years in jail” but would not back down from their campaign to “save democracy”.He further said that they follow the path shown by Mahatma Gandhi and continue to resist “peacefully and non-violently”, despite what he described as attempts by the state to intimidate them.The developments come amid the CJP-led campaign against the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The protesters have been demanding accountability from chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the exercise and have announced further mobilisation on October 10 in Delhi.
Article Summary: AISA national president Neha Bora claims that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacting to the claim said they would not be intimidated by the possibility of action under laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act.

Article Title: Ahead of CJP stir, Delhi Police asks DMRC to close 57 metro stations from 9pm
Article Text:
Proposed restrictions are scheduled to begin at 9 pm on Friday

The proposed restrictions would remain in force on October 10 until the situation returns to normal.The stations listed in the communication span several metro corridors and include Rajiv Chowk, Central Secretariat, Patel Chowk, Janpath, Mandi House, Supreme Court, New Delhi, Kashmere Gate, Jama Masjid, Chawri Bazar, Karol Bagh, Vishwavidyalaya, Hauz Khas, INA, Lajpat Nagar, Sarai Kale Khan-Nizamuddin, Jamia Millia Islamia, Okhla Vihar, Rithala, Rohini East, Rohini West, Shahdara, Welcome and Maujpur, among others.The list also includes stations such as Inderlok, Seelampur, Jafrabad, Yamuna Vihar, Azadpur, Majlis Park and Haiderpur Badli Mor.The police have requested the DMRC to issue necessary directions to the concerned officers and staff to implement appropriate measures.
Article Summary: Delhi Police requested the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation to consider closing the entry and exit gates of 57 metro stations from 9 pm on October 9. The police cited the possibility of unruly crowd movement towards sensitive locations. The proposed restrictions would remain in force on October 10 until the situation returns to normal.

Article Title: ‘Arrest me, detain me’: CJP's Abhijeet Dipke defies Delhi Police ban, says October 10 Jantar Mantar protest will go ahead
Article Text:
Cockroach Janta Party activist Abhijeet Dipke confirmed plans for a protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10.

Why Delhi Police denied permission





NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activist Abhijeet Dipke on Friday said the organisation would go ahead with its October 10 protest at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar despite Delhi Police denying permission, adding that its members were prepared to face arrest.Slamming the restrictions imposed ahead of the demonstration, Dipke questioned the decision to curtail public transport and said the measures would cause inconvenience to ordinary commuters.“What is this fear? Why are you this scared? You are scared of the youth in the country. You shut down trains, you shut down metro, what should one do?” he said.Dipke also questioned the government’s justification for the restrictions, arguing that shutting down metro services, cancelling trains and blocking roads would create the very inconvenience authorities cited as a concern.“Is Delhi a property of Narendra Modi or Amit Shah? Is this their ancestral property? Is this their paternal property? On one hand, you say that due to the protest, people are facing inconvenience, and on the other hand, you shut down all the metro, you shut down all the railways, you block all the roads. Now, won't there be inconvenience for people?” he said.Asserting that the activists would not back down, Dipke challenged the authorities to detain or arrest them.“How many people will they detain? Arrest me, detain me! Saurabh is ready, Ashutosh is ready. Arrest me, detain me!” he said.Dipke questioned the need for police permission to hold a demonstration at Jantar Mantar, which is a designated protest site. Referring to Article 19 of the Constitution, he argued that the proposed demonstration was an exercise of the activists’ constitutional rights.He also raised questions about Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and alleged changes relating to Form 6, asking why permission should be required to protest against the poll authority.“Did Gyanesh Kumar take permission? Before deleting 13 crore votes, did Gyanesh Kumar take permission? The Supreme Court didn't even give approval for the Form 6 modification. So, when Gyanesh Kumar, without telling anyone, without asking anyone, deletes 13 crore votes, then to protest against him, the constitutional right we have according to Article 19, what is the need for permission?” he said.Dipke further criticised the government over the restrictions, saying Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah should be concerned about the opposition being voiced by young people.“The government is very serious. I think Narendra Modi and Amit Shah should keep checking their blood pressure. The kind of fear this government is showing,” he said.Delhi Police has denied permission for the October 10 protest, citing the short notice, alleged non-compliance with directions during an earlier demonstration and concerns over public safety, law and order and traffic management.Joint commissioner of police Nupur Prasad said the New Delhi district received an application on October 7 from Saurabh Das, CJP co-convener, informing the police about the proposed demonstration seeking accountability from the Chief Election Commissioner.Prasad said the notice was submitted too close to the planned date, as the prescribed guidelines require applications to be received at least 10 days before a protest.She also alleged that CJP members had failed to comply with lawful directions and undertakings given during an earlier protest for which permission had been granted.“In the New Delhi area, Section 163 of the BNSS (Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita) is in operation, under which, to maintain public order and safety, a reasonable preventive restriction is in place,” Prasad said.She warned that legal action would be taken against anyone violating the provisions of Section 163 of the BNSS.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party activist Abhijeet Dipke confirms plans for protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10. Delhi Police has denied permission for the October 10 protest, citing the short notice, alleged non-compliance with directions during an earlier demonstration.

Article Title: Visually impaired Beed girl bags MBBS seat after HC intervention
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





An 18-year-old visually impaired girl from Beed, initially declared unfit to study medicine, has secured an MBBS seat after a legal battle in the Bombay High Court. The court’s intervention led to a fresh functional assessment that found her competent to pursue medical education.Syeda Musfira Fatema Rafiuddin has now been admitted to Govt Medical College, Sangli-Miraj.Musfira has congenital low vision caused by albinism, nystagmus and amblyopia. She scored 345 out of 720 in NEET-UG 2026 and secured an All-India OBC-NCL PwBD rank of 796.Her medical aspirations, however, hit a roadblock on Aug 10. The Medical Assessment Board at Sir JJ Group of Hospitals, Mumbai, declared her “ineligible for pursuing medical education”. It cited her visual condition and dependence on low-vision assistive devices.Musfira challenged the decision before the Aurangabad bench of the Bombay high court. Her counsel, advocate Sayyed Tauseef Yaseen, argued before a division bench of Justice Nitin B Suryawanshi and Justice Abasaheb D Shinde that the medical board had merely recorded her diagnosis.It had not conducted a functional or task-based assessment or considered reasonable accommodation, he submitted.Yaseen relied on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, and the Supreme Court judgment in Omkar Ramchandra Gond v Union of India. He argued that Musfira had already demonstrated her ability by competing in a rigorous national-level examination with prescribed magnifying aids. Her functional ability, rather than merely her diagnosis, should, therefore, have been assessed, he submitted.With NEET counselling underway, HC on Sept 22 directed Musfira to approach the appellate forum at Madras Medical College, Chennai, for an urgent reassessment.After evaluating her functional ability with low-vision aids, the appellate forum on Sept 25 declared her eligible and competent to pursue medical education under the PwBD category.A technical issue on the counselling portal then prevented Musfira from opting for the PwBD category. Yaseen approached the high court again on Sept 28. The authorities subsequently undertook to reopen the registration window for Musfira and facilitate her participation in the All-India and state counselling processes.She was subsequently allotted an MBBS seat at Govt Medical College, Sangli-Miraj, and granted admission.On Oct 1, Yaseen informed the high court that Musfira had secured admission. The bench then disposed of her petition as infructuous.
Article Summary: Syeda Musfira Fatema Rafiuddin has congenital low vision caused by albinism, nystagmus and amblyopia. She scored 345 out of 720 in NEET-UG 2026 and secured an All-India OBC-NCL PwBD rank of 796. The Medical Assessment Board at Sir JJ Group of Hospitals, Mumbai, declared her ‘ineligible for pursuing medical education’

Article Title: FIR against independent candidate for procession sans nod
Article Text:
The FIR has been registered at Begumpura police station

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





The city police have registered an FIR against independent candidate Ramesh Kasare Patil and 12 others for allegedly violating prohibitory orders by taking out a symbolic funeral procession on Tuesday afternoon.The FIR was registered at Begumpura police station under section 135 of the Maharashtra Police Act on the complaint of police constable Pandurang Gore.Patil allegedly joined a symbolic funeral procession at Chandane Chowk after filing his nomination for Aurangabad Graduate Constituency election around 11.30am on Tuesday. Inspector Pravina Yadav said Patil lay on a symbolic bier while an unlawful assembly held the procession near the MLC nomination venue.According to the FIR, Patil’s supporters also played drums and raised slogans during the procession. Police said no permission was granted to the candidate or his supporters to hold any agitation, procession or demonstration while filing the nomination. The procession allegedly violated the prohibitory order issued by police commissioner Pravin Pawar on Sept 30.The incident took place around 12.40pm on the road between Chandane Chowk and Annabhau Sathe Chowk, while the case was registered late on Tuesday. The other accused named in the FIR are Vilas Sonawane, Mahadev Amle, Bhagwat Kale, Ranganath Chapate, Santosh Jadhav, Nita Kale, Shivaji Sadge, Sitaram Naik, Sopan Kale, Sharad Galbe and Arun alias Chhotu Shrisundar.
Article Summary: Independent candidate Ramesh Kasare Patil and 12 others allegedly violated prohibitory orders by taking out a symbolic funeral procession on Tuesday afternoon. Article Title: Congress MLC & Mahayuti-led panel announce candidates for Gokul polls
Article Text:
Satej Patil announces Samvichari panel candidates for Gokul Dairy election

Kolhapur

:





Two coalition panels on Thursday announced 25 candidates each for elections in Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers Federation, popularly known as Gokul Dairy.In Mahayuti-led Chhatrapati Shahu Shetkari Vikas Aghadi, the prominent candidates are BJP’s Shoumika Mahadik, minister Hasan Mushrif’s son Navid Mushrif, former MLA Sujit Minchekar and Rajesh Patil. Most of the candidates have served as directors of Gokul Dairy in the past.On the other hand, Congress MLC Satej Patil-led Rajarshi Shahu Shetkari Samvichari Aghadi has announced prominent candidates such as Shashikant Patil Chuyekar, son of the founder of Gokul Dairy, Anandrao Patil Chuyekar, former MLA Raju Awale, former Kolhapur ZP vice-president Shashikant Khot and most of the candidates are associated with cooperative institutions.The announcement of ‘Samvichari Aghadi’ was held in the presence of Patil, ex-MP Raju Shetti, Peasants and Workers Party leader Jayant Patil, Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Vijay Devane and NCP(SP)’s VB Patil. Satej Patil also announced the manifesto of Samvichari Aghadi, which will be taken to around 5,300 voters who are delegates of the primary milk societies. “We have decided to increase Gokul Dairy’s collection of milk from 20 lakh litres per day to 30 lakh litres per day.We would increase the price by at least Rs5 per litre for buffalo milk and Rs2 per litre for cow milk. Also, the price of cattle feed would be reduced by Rs 100 per sack within the first month,” said Patil.Patil announced that Shashikant Patil Chuyekar would be made chairperson of Gokul if Samvichari Aghadi gets a majority.Raju Shetti said CM Devendra Fadnavis ’s flagship Nagpur-Goa Shaktipeeth Expressway project will be one of the key issues over which the election for Gokul will be fought. “The highway would destroy the rural economy. Sugarcane crop would suffer, followed by the industries that depend on it,” said Shetti.The panels will get their symbols on Friday. The voting is scheduled for Oct 18.
Article Summary: Two coalition panels on Thursday announced 25 candidates each for elections in Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers Federation. Most of the candidates have served as directors of Gokul Dairy in the past. The panels will get their symbols on Friday. The voting is scheduled for Oct 18.

Article Title: Gokul poll: NCP gets 9 seats, BJP & Sena 7 each, and JSSP 2
Article Text:
Mahayuti politicians discuss seat sharing for Gokul election

Kolhapur

:





After several rounds of closed-door negotiations and bickering, Mahayuti functionaries in Kolhapur on Wednesday finalised a seat-sharing pact for the Oct 18 election to the Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers Federation, popularly known as Gokul.The cooperative dairy, which has an annual turnover of around Rs 3,000 crore, elects 25 directors every five years.Announcing the formula after a meeting on Wednesday evening, BJP minister Chandrakant Patil said, “NCP is going to contest on nine seats, and BJP and Shiv Sena on seven seats each. Jansurajya Shakti Party has two seats. Minister Hasan Mushrif will announce the list of our 25 candidates on Thursday on social media,” Patil said. NCP is expected to accommodate the front led by Shirol MLA Rajendra Patil Yadravkar from its quota.Having settled the arithmetic, Mahayuti now faces a tougher challenge: convincing a large number of ticket aspirants to withdraw. Several supporters have filed nominations hoping to find a place on the alliance panel.Mushrif acknowledged the difficult task ahead before heading into the nearly three-hour meeting with Mahayuti politicians at a Kolhapur hotel.“I have experienced a night before finalising candidates for last five decades. One should take the tough call, try to convince the supporters to withdraw,” he said.Meanwhile, Congress MLC Satej Patil, who was expected to announce his panel against Mahayuti on Wednesday, deferred the announcement to Thursday afternoon. Sources said he could seek to tap discontent among Mahayuti aspirants left out of the final panel to strengthen his challenge.
Article Summary: Mahayuti functionaries in Kolhapur on Wednesday finalised a seat-sharing pact for the Oct 18 election. NCP is expected to accommodate the front led by Shirol MLA Rajendra Patil Yadravkar from its quota. Mahayuti now faces a tougher challenge: convincing a large number of ticket aspirants to withdraw.

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Article Title: Man in Mahindra Thar with duplicate plate molests woman, knocks down another in Kharghar
Article Text:
30-year-old man was apprehended for allegedly molesting a woman and injuring another in Navi Mumbai.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team within 10 hours on Thursday evening.He had allegedly molested a 26-year-old woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night and, an hour later, severely injured a 22-year-old woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, Kharghar.Acting on a complaint by the woman allegedly molested by the Thar SUV driver, Kharghar police registered an FIR under BNS section 74 for the offence of assault or criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty.While, as per the complaint by the injured woman Shrawani Dandekar, a resident of sector 3, Belpada, an FIR under relevant BNS sections and Motor Vehicle Act was registered against the Thar SUV driver for rash and negligent driving causing hurt.The detained aaccused identified as Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of sector 50, Seawoods, Nerul was handed over to Kharghar police for further legal action.Previously, in January 2021, he was arrested by Nerul police in the FIR registered against him for alleged kidnapping, sexual harassment and molestation of a woman.Sanjay Joshi, senior inspector of Kharghar said, "The accused Nakhvi has been detained and subsequently it will be decided whether to arrest him or serve with a notice under Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) for cooperating in police investigating."Audumbar Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-3 said, "After an FIR for molestation was registered at Kharghar police station by the victim woman, a resident of sector 34, Kharghar. As per the orders of higher authority, our team started a parallel probe. From the CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we obtained the red Thar SUV's registration number, which was of Vashi RTO passing.""When verified, the registration number was found to be that of a Maruti WagonR car. As the accused had used a duplicate registration number plate, we scrutinized as many as 62 Thar SUVs registered with various Regional Transport Offices (RTOs). Subsequently, we obtained the registration number of a red Thar SUV that was registered with Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar RTO," Patil added.SPI Patil further informed, "The SUV was registered in the name of Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of Devaki Apartment in sector-50, Seawoods. From his mobile number registered with the RTO, his location was tracked.""He was apprehended from Bonkode village, Koparkhairane on Thursday late evening. Upon thorough interrogation, he confessed that he had inappropriately touched the woman pedestrian near Pethpada metro station while he drove his Thar SUV and sped away. He even confessed to have injured a woman pedestrian by hitting her his SUV while driving in Belpada area," he said.
Article Summary: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team on Thursday evening. He had allegedly molested a woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night. An hour later, he severely injured a woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, KharGHar.

Article Title: Thane Shiv Sena (UBT) leader murder: 2 more arrested near Alibag while fleeing to Goa, total 3
Article Text:
Two additional suspects were arrested in connection with the murder of Shiv Sena division chief Pradeep Purnekar.





THANE: The Thane Crime Branch has arrested two more accused in connection with the murder of Shiv Sena (UBT) division chief Pradeep alias Balu Purnekar, taking the total number of arrests in the case to three.The arrested accused have been identified as Nikhil Yadav and Nitesh Pawar alias Bhavdya. The two were apprehended near Alibag while allegedly attempting to flee towards Goa, according to police sources.The Crime Branch reportedly traced the duo following information obtained during the questioning of suspects detained earlier in the case. Police teams had been searching for the accused after Purnekar was shot and attacked with a sharp-edged weapon at his office in Thane.According to investigators, Yadav allegedly opened fire on Purnekar, while Pawar allegedly attacked him with a sharp weapon. Police are now expected to question both accused to establish the sequence of events, the motive and the role of others involved in the alleged conspiracy.The two accused are expected to be produced before the Thane Sessions Court on Friday. Police will also attempt to recover the weapons allegedly used in the murder and investigate how the accused obtained them.Earlier, Prakash alias Papya Shinde was arrested in connection with the case. The police have also formed a Special Investigation Team (SIT) headed by DCP (Crime) Amarsingh Jadhav to conduct a detailed probe into the killing.The investigation is continuing, with police probing the alleged conspiracy, the role of other suspects and the possible involvement of the absconding accused.
Article Summary: The arrested accused have been identified as Nikhil Yadav and Nitesh Pawar alias Bhavdya. The two were apprehended near Alibag while allegedly attempting to flee towards Goa. Police are now expected to question both accused to establish the sequence of events, the motive and the role of others involved.

Article Title: Disha Salian case: Father, lawyer seek police protection, allege threats from Sena (UBT) leaders
Article Text:
Ojha questioned Aaditya Thackeray’s ‘Y-plus’ security, saying those who raised the issue and allegedly faced threats remained unprotected.

(With agency inputs)





THANE: Advocate Nilesh Ojha on Sunday said that Disha Salian’s father, Satish Salian, Sameer Wankhede, Ashutosh Pathak and he have sought police protection, alleging that they received threats from Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders.Ojha, who is representing Satish Salian in the case, said they have written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah, the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), the Chief Justice of India and Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, seeking protection."The CBI FIR was registered, and a letter was immediately written requesting police protection for four individuals: Satish Salian, our witness Sameer Wankhede, myself, and Ashutosh Pathak, " Ojha told news agency ANI.Ojha questioned the provision of ‘Y-plus’ security to Aaditya Thackeray , saying those who brought the matter to light and allegedly faced threats had been left without protection."The letter clearly states, citing records from your Home Ministry and the Narcotics Bureau, that it is evident that Aditya Thackeray is involved in the drug trade. Furthermore, an FIR has now been registered against him regarding gang rape, murder, and a cover-up.Several other high-profile individuals and police officers are also implicated as accused in this matter," he said."We have already provided all prima facie evidence; the CBI has obtained everything necessary during the investigation to secure a conviction. Yet, the accused currently enjoys 'Y-plus' security provided by your administration. Meanwhile, those who brought this matter to light and those facing direct threats from individuals like Sanjay Raut were left unprotected," the advocate added.He further said that providing security was mandatory under the Witness Protection Scheme and Supreme Court guidelines, and alleged that their request for protection had not been acted upon.He further added, "Providing security is mandatory under the Witness Protection Scheme and Supreme Court guidelines. Yet, they failed to do so. Consequently, we compiled all the material and handed it over to the CBI. We also urged them to investigate the role of Police Commissioner Deven Bharti and determine why police protection was not granted.""We have given a copy of this to the CBI, along with Prime Minister Modi ji, the Home Minister, the Chief Justice of India, and the Chief Minister," Ojha said.Disha Salian was found dead in Mumbai on June 8, 2020. Her death was initially registered as an Accidental Death Report (ADR).Salian died days before actor Sushant Singh Rajput , whose death also led to a high-profile investigation and widespread public controversy.Bombay High Court directed the CBI to register a formal First Information Report (FIR) and launch a fresh probe.As the probe progresses, Satish Salian, accompanied by his lawyer Nilesh Ojha, has submitted a pen drive containing material they described as evidence related to Disha Salian’s death.Meanwhile, Aaditya Thackeray has denied the allegations and responded to the defamation notice issued by Satish Salian.
Article Summary: Disha Salian’s father, Satish Salian, Sameer Wankhede, Ashutosh Pathak and he have sought police protection. They allege that they received threats from Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders. Ojha questioned the provision of ‘Y-plus’ security to Aaditya Thackeray. He said those who raised the issue and allegedly faced threats remained unprotected.

Article Title: 14 AISF women members detained in Itarsi while travelling to Delhi for CJP protest, lodged in hotel
Article Text:
Fourteen women affiliated with the All India Students' Federation were detained at Itarsi railway station during their journey





PUNE: Fourteen women members of the All India Students’ Federation (AISF), travelling from Pune to Delhi to participate in a protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, were detained at Itarsi railway station in Madhya Pradesh on Thursday evening amid security measures ahead of the protest called by CJP.The students were travelling aboard the Goa Express when they were intercepted by police at the key railway junction. They were subsequently taken to a local hotel and kept in a banquet hall under restricted access.Speaking to The Times of India, hotel general manager Deepak Chaudhary confirmed that the students had been brought to the premises between 6pm and 7pm.“The students were brought in between 6pm and 7pm and they have been secluded in a banquet hall, with no staff allowed to enter the area,” Chaudhary said, adding that food and water had been provided to them as instructed by the authorities.Shravni Duwa from AISF Pune is one of the protestors detained at Itarsi.She said, "around 5.45pm police entered our train going to Delhi at Itarsi junction railway station and screamed and shouted at us and in the scuffle clothes were torn and a woman even injured and bruised her leg. We were then taken to this hotel where we have been kept detained for the last 18 hours now without letting us talk to our lawyers or see any doctor."
Article Summary: Fourteen women affiliated with the All India Students' Federation were detained at Itarsi railway station during their journey. They were travelling from Pune to Delhi to participate in a protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The students were intercepted by police at the key railway junction.

Article Title: CM Fadnavis, deputy CM Shinde’s visit to Delhi to get political directions and not for drought relief, claims opposition
Article Text:
CM Devendra Fadnavis

Pune:





The opposition has criticised Mahayuti govt over chief minister Devendra Fadnavis and deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde ’s recent visits to Delhi, claiming that their meetings with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah were aimed at seeking political directions rather than securing relief for drought-affected people in the state.After meeting Shah on Wednesday, Fadnavis said he had apprised the home minister of the drought situation and requested a relief package through National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF). Before Fadnavis’s visit, Shinde was in Delhi on Tuesday, where he held a meeting with PM Modi. Shinde said the Centre had assured the state of all necessary assistance to mitigate the drought situation.The opposition, however, claimed that both the chief minister and deputy chief minister had failed to provide immediate relief to farmers in distress.“These meetings of Fadnavis and Shinde with Modi and Shah show that the state is being controlled from Delhi. The agenda of their meetings was not to discuss measures to tackle the drought situation but to seek political directions, which is quite unfortunate,” said state Congress chief Harshwardhan Sapkal.State govt declared drought in 265 tehsils on Sept 26, following which the panchnama process was started in the affected villages.“Survival has become a challenge for the farming community, but state govt is busy with politics. Instead of providing relief to farmers, the govt is busy shielding those responsible for the paper leak,” said Congress MLA Vijay Wadettiwar.A Central govt committee will review the drought situation in the state, and based on its report, a drought relief package is likely to be announced. Opposition members said that despite the chief minister and deputy chief minister’s visits to Delhi, the process of providing relief had not been expedited.“Eknath Shinde said he had a half-hour discussion with the prime minister, but he has not specified when farmers would get the actual relief. Despite these meetings, the Centre’s team still took time to arrive in the state for the inspection. Shinde admitted that 85% of crops had been lost, but he has not announced any compensation. If the chief minister and deputy chief minister have failed to provide any relief to farmers, what is the use of their Delhi visits?” said Shiv Sena (UBT) senior leader Ambadas Danve.Fadnavis said state govt would provide relief without waiting for the Centre’s package and said farmers had never received drought relief so early in the past.“Since 2001, drought has never been declared in Oct. It was always declared by the end of Nov or in Dec. This is the first time it has been declared in Sept, and state govt has worked out a package that will be released at the earliest,” Fadnavis said.
Article Summary: Mahayuti govt criticised over chief minister Devendra Fadnavis and deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde ’s recent visits to Delhi. Opposition claims that their meetings with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah were aimed at seeking political directions.

Article Title: Oppn marches against CEC, demands transparency in poll process
Article Text:
Activists of Congress, NCP(Sharad Pawar), Shiv Sena(UBT) and Communist partiesprotested at Variety Square inNagpur on Thursday

Nagpur/Amravati/Chandrapur:





Opposition parties of the INDIA bloc on Thursday staged protests in Nagpur, Chandrapur and Amravati against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, alleging that the functioning of Election Commission of India (ECI) had undermined transparency in the electoral process.In Nagpur, leaders and workers of Congress , NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar), Shiv Sena (Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray), CPI and CPM took out a march from Mahatma Gandhi statue to the district collectorate. A delegation submitted a memorandum to the administration outlining their objections to the functioning of ECI and seeking greater transparency in electoral processes.The protesters raised slogans against Kumar, while also expressing solidarity with leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi . Former Maharashtra home minister Anil Deshmukh, former minister Sunil Kedar, Nagpur city Congress president Prafulla Gudadhe, Nagpur rural Congress president Ashwin Bais, Avantika Lekurwale, NCP city president Duneswar Pethe and office-bearers and workers of Thackeray-led Shiv Sena were also present.In Chandrapur, Congress MP Pratibha Dhanorkar demanded Kumar’s resignation while addressing the party’s ‘Vote Bachao–Desh Bachao’ agitation, organised as part of its ‘Loktantra Bachao Week’. Congress workers marched from Gandhi Chowk to the district collectorate, where a delegation submitted a memorandum addressed to President Droupadi Murmu .Dhanorkar described the campaign as an effort to protect voters’ rights, constitutional values and the independence and impartiality of Election Commission.District Congress president and former MLA Subhash Dhote said Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi and the INDIA bloc were raising issues concerning democratic rights and urged citizens to remain vigilant.In Amravati, opposition parties marched to the district collectorate, where a delegation submitted a memorandum to collector Ashish Yerekar. Former minister Yashomati Thakur criticised the BJP-led govt and Election Commission, alleging that the electoral process had been compromised.MP Balwant Wankhade, former minister Sunil Deshmukh, Congress rural president Bablu Deshmukh, former MLA Virendra Jagtap, city Congress president Bablu Shekhawat and NCP (SP) district president Anil Jalamkar were among those who led the protest.
Article Summary: Opposition parties of the INDIA bloc staged protests in Nagpur, Chandrapur and Amravati against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. They alleged that the functioning of Election Commission of India (ECI) had undermined transparency in the electoral process.

Article Title: Tamil Nadu Congress condemns Rahul Gandhi’s arrest, demands removal of CEC
Article Text:
TNCC senior leaders and cadres stage a demonstration in Chennai on Thursday, protesting the arrest of Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders and MPs in Delhi. The protesters were detained while marching to the Election Commission demanding the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of voter-roll manipulation.

Chennai:





Tamil Nadu Congress Committee on Thursday held a protest in Chennai condemning the arrest of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and INDIA bloc MPs for organising an agitation demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Congress said INDIA bloc would organise protest meetings across Tamil Nadu on Oct 13 and 14 against the CEC.At the protest on Anna Salai in Chennai, TNCC functionaries raised slogans against Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah , accusing BJP-led Union govt of using force to suppress the Opposition. Congress functionaries burnt an effigy and posters carrying images of Modi, Shah and Kumar, causing temporary traffic congestion in the area.The protesters demanded Kumar’s immediate removal, alleging the deletion of 13 crore names from the electoral rolls through SIR across the country was an “unlawful act.”Former TNCC president Thirunavukkarasar said Congress and its allies would continue their agitation until Kumar was removed or resigned. He said Opposition parties were considering measures like approaching Supreme Court seeking Kumar’s removal and moving a resolution in the parliament in this regard when the parliament meets.“Congress will not rest until Gyanesh Kumar is removed from office. Rahul Gandhi has made it clear that the agitation will continue until he is removed,” Thirunavukkarasar said.TN Congress legislature party leader Tharahai Cuthbert, senior leader Peter Alphonse and several other functionaries attended the demo, while ministers Rajesh Kumar and P Viswanathan did not turn up for the demo.
Article Summary: Protesters were detained while marching to the Election Commission demanding the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of voter-roll manipulation. Congress functionaries burnt an effigy and posters carrying images of Modi, Shah and Kumar, causing temporary traffic congestion in the area.

Article Title: Dharapuram bypoll: EVMs, VVPATs secured under two-tier armed cover, 24x7 CCTV surveillance
Article Text:
Representative image





TIRUPUR: Electronic voting machines (EVMs) and voter verifiable paper audit trail (VVPAT) units used for the Dharapuram assembly byelection in Tirupur district have been placed in a strong room under two-tier armed security and round-the-clock CCTV surveillance, officials said.After the completion of polling on Oct 6, the EVMs and VVPAT units were brought to the counting centre located at LRG Govt Women’s Arts College in the district.District election officer and collector Dr Manish Narnaware and election general observer Chinmay Pundlikrao Gotmare, IAS, on Wednesday supervised the placement of machines into the strong room in the presence of candidates and their agents. The strong room was sealed thereafter, with the participation of superintendent of police Srishti Singh, IPS, deputy commissioner of police Akash Joshi, IPS, and Dharapuram revenue divisional officer A Felix Raja.Narnaware said the strong room would be opened on Oct 9 -- the counting day -- in the presence of candidates or their representatives and the central observer, under videography.District election authorities said the strong room was being protected with armed security personnel in a two-tier arrangement, with continuous monitoring through CCTV cameras.To ensure uninterrupted supervision of CCTV feeds, three officers of deputy collector rank have been deployed daily at the district level, while separate monitoring officers have been appointed for the assembly constituency.The monitoring will continue until the counting day on Oct 9.Authorities said all contesting candidates have been informed in writing about appointing representatives to observe the security arrangements, with permission granted for such representatives to stay outside the inner security cordon.Polling was held at 320 booths in the constituency. There are 2,23,306 registered voters, and 1,79,214 votes were cast, recording a turnout of 80.25%.
Article Summary: Electronic voting machines used for Dharapuram assembly byelection in Tirupur district. EVMs and VVPAT units placed in strong room under two-tier armed security and round-the-clock CCTV surveillance. The monitoring will continue until the counting day on Oct 9.

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.
Article Summary: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district. Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid.

Article Title: Death sentence on preacher for sexual assault on minor girls referred to HC
Article Text:
Death sentence on preacher for sexual assault on minor girls referred to HC

Madurai

:





The death sentence imposed on a preacher for sexually assaulting four minor girls in Tirunelveli was referred to Madras high court for confirmation on Thursday.The case of the prosecution is that Abraham, 47, a preacher, sexually assaulted the girls at his church, during music classes and at deserted places in their neighbourhood. The abuse came to light in 2022 after an eight-year-old girl complained of pain in her private parts. Her mother took her to a hospital, where she learnt that the child had been sexually assaulted.Three other girls from the same extended family told their mothers that Abraham had also sexually assaulted them from the Covid-19 lockdown in 2020 to 2022. In 2022, police registered a case for offences under Pocso Act and arrested Abraham.In August, the special court for exclusive trial of cases under Pocso Act in Tirunelveli convicted Abraham and imposed the death sentence on him. Since the death sentence was imposed by the trial court, the same was referred to HC for confirmation.A division bench of Justice M Nirmal Kumar and Justice N Gunasekaran posted the referred trial case for hearing on October 30.
Article Summary: The case of the prosecution is that Abraham, 47, a preacher, sexually assaulted the girls at his church, during music classes and at deserted places in their neighbourhood. The abuse came to light in 2022 after an eight-year-old girl complained of pain in her private parts. In 2022, police registered a case for offences under Pocso Act and arrested Abraham.

Article Title: Four held with ₹2 lakh counterfeit currency in Madurai
Article Text: Madurai: Four men were arrested after police seized counterfeit ₹500 notes worth ₹2 lakh during a vehicle check near Pudupatti tank bund on Thursday. Police said the suspects, travelling in an autorickshaw, tried to flee on spotting officers. The notes carried identical serial numbers and were intended for circulation. Those arrested were Premkumar , 50, Christopher Mathiyazhagan, 32, Karthik , 32, and Maheswaran, 35. Police also seized a computer, printer and chemicals allegedly used to produce the counterfeit currency.
Article Summary: The notes carried identical serial numbers and were intended for circulation. Police also seized a computer, printer and chemicals allegedly used to produce the counterfeit currency. Those arrested were Premkumar, 50, Christopher Mathiyazhagan, 32, Karthik, 32, and Maheswaran, 35.

Article Title: Traffic affected on Salem-Madurai National Highway after trailer truck crashes near Rasipuram
Article Text: NAMAKKAL: Traffic was affected for more than an hour on the Salem-Madurai National Highway near Rasipuram in Namakkal district on Thursday afternoon after a trailer truck crashed while descending the Andagalur Gate flyover.No casualties or injuries were reported.The truck was carrying about 60 tonnes of steel angles from Maharashtra to Karur. An officer at the Rasipuram police station said the driver lost control of the vehicle while descending the flyover around 1.30pm. The truck hit a streetlight pole on the roadside. “The vehicle partially blocked the road, causing congestion and delays for motorists and commuters,” he said.Vehicles piled up for two kilometres on the NH. The Rasipuram police reached the spot after receiving information, regulated traffic and moved the truck to the roadside.Police registered a case and were investigating the circumstances leading to the crash.
Article Summary: Trailer truck crashes on Salem-Madurai National Highway near Rasipuram. Truck was carrying 60 tonnes of steel angles from Maharashtra to Karur. Driver lost control of the vehicle while descending the flyover. No casualties or injuries were reported.
